subject: chemistry
title: Crude oil, hydrocarbons and alkanes
key_idea: Crude oil is a finite mixture of many hydrocarbons, formed from the remains of ancient plankton. Most of the hydrocarbons are alkanes, which have only single bonds and the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. The first four are methane, ethane, propane and butane.

blocks.text: This section covers where crude oil comes from and what it contains.

items.meaning: A mixture of a very large number of compounds, found in rocks.
A compound made of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.
A resource that will run out because it is used faster than it forms.

items: It is the remains of ancient biomass, mainly **plankton**.
The plankton died and was buried in mud.
Over millions of years it was compressed, which formed crude oil in rocks.

diagram.alt: Plankton dies, is buried in mud, is compressed over millions of years and becomes crude oil.

blocks.text: What it contains and why it matters

items: Most of the compounds are hydrocarbons, and most of those are alkanes.
The carbon atoms in the molecules are in chains or rings.
It is a source of fuels such as petrol, kerosene and diesel oil.
It is also the feedstock for the petrochemical industry, which makes useful materials such as solvents, lubricants, polymers and detergents.
Modern life depends on hydrocarbons for transport fuels and for many everyday materials.
Petrol, kerosene and diesel oil are non-renewable fossil fuels. Methane is a non-renewable fossil fuel found in natural gas.
Crude oil is a finite resource made from ancient plankton buried in mud.
It is a mixture of many compounds, most of them hydrocarbons.
It supplies fuels and feedstock for the petrochemical industry.

blocks.text: Alkanes are the main hydrocarbons in crude oil. They all fit one general formula.

items.meaning: A hydrocarbon with only single bonds between its carbon atoms.
Having only single covalent bonds between carbon atoms, so no more atoms can be added.
A drawing that shows every atom and every covalent bond.

blocks.label: General formula of the alkanes
where: n is the number of carbon atoms in the molecule
2n + 2 is the number of hydrogen atoms in the molecule

blocks.text: The first four alkanes have 1 to 4 carbon atoms. Each name ends in -ane.

items: Methane, displayed: one carbon atom joined to four hydrogen atoms by single bonds.
Ethane, displayed: two carbon atoms joined by a single bond, each also bonded to three hydrogen atoms.
In a displayed formula each carbon atom forms four single bonds.
Each hydrogen atom forms one bond.
Every C–C bond is a single bond, so alkanes are saturated.

diagram.alt: Practise working out the number of hydrogen atoms in an alkane from its number of carbon atoms.
diagram.question: An alkane molecule has **{n}** carbon atoms. Work out the number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule.

items: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
The first four are methane, ethane, propane and butane.
Check a formula by counting: hydrogen atoms = 2 × carbon atoms + 2.

checks.q: Describe how crude oil was formed.
checks.a: It is the remains of ancient plankton (biomass). The plankton was buried in mud and compressed over millions of years.

checks.q: Explain why propane, C₃H₈, is a hydrocarbon and an alkane.
checks.a: It contains carbon and hydrogen atoms only, so it is a hydrocarbon. It has only single bonds and fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so it is an alkane.

checks.q: How many hydrogen atoms are in a molecule of an alkane with 10 carbon atoms?

worked_example.question:
Some fractions of crude oil are processed to produce fuel for transport.

Describe how crude oil was formed.
answer_points: Plankton (or the remains of ancient biomass) died.
They were buried (in mud, or by sediments).
This happened over millions of years.
worked_example.tip: Each point is one mark. Say plankton or ancient biomass, and mention the long time.

worked_example.question:
Crude oil is a complex mixture of substances.

Most of the substances in crude oil are alkanes.
Explain why alkanes are described as hydrocarbons.
answer_points: They contain hydrogen and carbon atoms.
They contain hydrogen and carbon atoms only.
worked_example.tip: The second mark depends on the first, so give both ideas in one clear sentence.

items: Recall the formulae of methane, ethane, propane and butane and draw their structures showing all covalent bonds.
Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons because every bond between their carbon atoms is a single bond.
A saturated molecule has no double bond, so it holds the maximum number of hydrogen atoms.

worked_example.question:
This question is about hydrocarbons.

Ethane is a saturated hydrocarbon.

Explain why ethane is called both a hydrocarbon and saturated.
answer_points: Hydrocarbon because it contains only carbon and hydrogen.
Saturated because it contains single (covalent) bonds only.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each word. Fitting the formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ is also accepted for hydrocarbon.

worked_example.question: State the meaning of the term hydrocarbon.
answer_points: A compound containing carbon and hydrogen only.

blocks.text: The three fossil fuels are **coal**, **natural gas** and **petroleum** (crude oil).

items: Methane is the main constituent of natural gas.
Petroleum is a mixture of hydrocarbons.

worked_example.question:
The table shows the molecular formulae of six organic compounds, A, B, C, D, E and F.

A: C₂H₄
B: C₂H₆
C: C₃H₆
D: C₃H₈
E: C₄H₈
F: C₄H₁₀

Explain which homologous series compound B belongs to.
answer_points: Because its formula fits the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (C₂H₆ has 2 × 2 + 2 = 6 hydrogen atoms).
worked_example.tip: The second mark can be scored even if the series is wrong or missing.

blocks.text: The fifth alkane is **pentane**, with five carbon atoms.

items: Molecular formula: C₅H₁₂.
Structural formula: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃.
Displayed: a chain of five carbon atoms joined by single bonds, with hydrogen atoms completing four bonds on each carbon.
